guarantees.text: A suspicion is not proof, so by default a flagged column is reported and the run goes on; with `leakage_policy="block"` any flagged column blocks the run.
The plan gives a reason for every technique it includes, rejects or defers.
Ambiguous targets, unparseable times, too few groups or minority examples, impossible constraints and rejected approvals put the run in `BLOCKED` instead of guessing.

Bundles are pickle-based, so loading is refused unless the HMAC signature verifies or you pass `trusted=True`; checksums are verified before anything is unpickled ([`docs/SECURITY.md`](docs/SECURITY.md)).

CPU / time / memory limits are enforced: the first trial always runs, so a result exists, and no later trial starts past the time budget or the memory limit; under the default hard enforcement every trial runs in a supervised process that is killed at a hard time ceiling or when its resident memory exceeds the limit.

`python -m benchmarks.reliability` checks nine properties on synthetic data with known answers: same seed gives the same result, replay agrees, noise labels score near a ROC AUC of 0.5, a planted leak is found, signed bundles round-trip and reject tampering, 90% intervals cover, drift is flagged only when real, and one crashing candidate cannot sink a run.

Titanic's near-perfect score comes from leaked columns (`boat`, `body`): the leakage screen flags both (`boat` by skill, missingness and record purity; `body` by record purity only, because it is recorded for 9% of passengers, all of whom died), and `leakage_policy="block"` (opt-in; the default is `"warn"`) refuses to proceed.
Third-party adapters can also register via the `scmle.models` entry-point group and must pass `scmle.models.conformance.comply`.
No underscore-prefixed names anywhere, enforced by `tests/unit/test_conventions.py`.
* The HTTP serving adapter is a minimal reference server: it verifies bearer tokens when configured (and refuses a non-loopback bind without them) but has no TLS; terminate TLS at an ingress.
* `gpu="required"` blocks a run unless PyTorch can see a CUDA device.
`tests/unit/test_qualification_api_rule.py` enforces both halves.

`leakage_policy` keeps its values and its meaning at the top level (`Project(...)` and the snapshot in `tests/fixtures/public_api.json` are unchanged); what blocks is now a typed result, `Portrait.blockers`, from the permutation screen in `scmle.assurance.admissibility.screen`.

Behaviour changes that users may notice: in a run every suspect may block, for binary, multiclass and regression targets alike, whatever the state of the certificates, which are evidence and decide nothing (an earlier version blocked only on a mechanism with a passing certificate, which was binary classification alone), the screen also reports a value recorded only for some outcomes when most rows are blank, and `Portrait` gained the optional field `leakage` (default empty) and its `to_dict` key.

Charter format 8 adds the optional `entity` and `reconcile` sub-blocks of `ingest` (`scmle.assurance.charter.ingest.Entity`, `Expectation`, extension surfaces); a format 7 ingest charter keeps its hash and signature.

Charter format 9 adds the optional `subgroups` field of the causal block (`scmle.assurance.charter.causal.Subgroup`, an extension surface) and the optional `attestors` and `attestations` fields (`scmle.assurance.charter.causal.Attestor`, `scmle.causal.identification.attest`); a format 4 causal charter keeps its hash and signature.

Charter format 10 adds the optional `uncertainty` block (`scmle.assurance.charter.uncertainty.Uncertainty`, an extension surface; the snapshot is unchanged); a charter of format 9 or older keeps its hash and signature.

Charter format 11 adds the optional `coverage_on_confirmation` field of the `uncertainty` block (`scmle.assurance.charter.uncertainty.Uncertainty`, an extension surface; a format 10 charter keeps its hash and signature, both pinned).
A charter run with a decision block now also writes `decision_report.json`, `policy_value.json` and, with a rollout plan, `rollout_design.json` and `rollout_decisions.jsonl`.

`scmle.assurance.charter.contracts.AnalysisEstimand` gained the optional field `causal` (`scmle.assurance.charter.causal.Question`, with `Control` and `Confounding`); it is omitted from the record when unset, so charters of format 1 to 3 keep their hash and signature, and a charter that carries it is format 4 (an older wrapper carrying it is refused).

`choose_decision_threshold` takes the threshold from the charter's cost model when the charter has a decision block and the task is binary, even if `decision.threshold_objective` is `none`; without a block it behaves as before.
`evaluation.json` gained the keys `net_benefit` (null without a block) and, inside `decision`, `f11`.
The snapshot's `surfaces` block pins the signature of each name above, and `scripts/check_api_compatibility.py` reports `surface added`, `surface removed` and `surface contract changed` for it.
The spec format is versioned (`SPEC_FORMAT`); `from_dict` refuses any other format.

`scmle.security.tokens`, `scmle.security.access` and `scmle.security.audit` are extension surfaces like `scmle.deploy.contract`: token verification (`Verifier`, `Keystore`, `Key`, `RevocationList`, `Principal`), the request gateway (`Gateway`, `RateLimiter`, `DeniedError`) and the audit log (`Log`) are pinned in the snapshot's `surfaces` block.

Behaviour changes to existing classes: `HttpServing` gained the keyword-only `gateway` and refuses a non-loopback `host` without one; `ModalityHttpServing` kept its constructor, gained `protect`, and `start` refuses a non-loopback `host` without a gateway.
`scmle.data.store` (`objectstore`, `snapshot`, `quality`, `processing`) and `scmle.runtime.retry` are extension surfaces pinned in the snapshot's `surfaces` block.

The package layering (format 4) and the class renames before it (format 3) changed the module path and class name stored inside every bundle, so a bundle written by an earlier build (format 3, 2 or 1) cannot be loaded or migrated: `Bundle.load` refuses it with an error that says to retrain and save again.
A bundle whose pickled members name a module or class this build does not have is refused the same way, with `ArtifactError`.
**Plan** asks the `Planner` (a chain of `Refiner`s) for candidates, recording every included, rejected and deferred technique.
* **Resource governor** applies CPU / time / memory limits and reports, per limit, how it was enforced and what was observed.
Statistics about tables (counts, distinct counts, keys, inclusion) are aggregate queries run in the source, because a sample cannot confirm a universal statement.
Rows are pulled only by `profile.untorn`, which needs a total order and rejects a read whose snapshot token or rows changed.

Another table is read only through `asof_view.View.visible`, which returns rows recorded at or before the target row's cutoff; `synthesize` imports no connector or reader, so it never reads a table except through a view.
What the view cannot know is whether the recorded time is true, so every feature carries the weakest tier among the tables it reads.
A charter run with an `ingest` block calls it (`scmle.core.ingest_stage`); when the block carries an `entity` sub-block the resolved entity becomes the split's group column.
* Confidence intervals on the test metric resample the independent units of observation (rows, whole groups, or contiguous time blocks).

Per candidate column it computes a cross-fitted held-out skill (AUC, or R^2 for a continuous target) with an exact permutation p-value, permuting within groups or time blocks when they are known; a missing-value test against the target (Fisher or chi-square with Cramer's V, or the permutation scheme with groups); and a record-purity test for a value captured only for some outcomes.

Guaranteed: under the null of no association, and conditional on the model and fold choices, the chance of any false alarm is at most `alpha`, and the false discovery rate of the significant list is at most `alpha` under arbitrary dependence between columns.
`leakage_policy="block"` (opt-in; the default is `warn`) blocks the run on any suspect, and on a screen that could not check its columns.
Called directly (`screen.screen`, without gates), the screen is descriptive: a suspect is reported with its p-values as a warning and nothing is blocked.
An adapter from the `scmle.models` entry point, or an estimator added with `register_estimator`, must pass `scmle.models.conformance.comply` or it is not registered.
Readers take a snapshot: `Catalog.stock` copies the user adapters once, and `Repertoire` replaces its tables rather than editing them, so a run that is scoring never sees a metric vanish halfway.
Registry locks are never held while a user estimator runs, but a `Maintainer.review` holds its state lock for the whole retrain.
`diagnostics/decision_log.json` | The evidence behind each choice (what was included, rejected, deferred).

`dataset_manifest.json`, `dataset_profile.json`, `dataset_card.json` | Row and column counts, hashes, resolved column kinds and findings. `dataset_profile.json` also holds `leakage`: the leakage screen's level, family size, suspects and the suspects that may block a run (in a run every suspect may block, whatever the state of the certificates).
`custody_log.jsonl` | With `--charter`: a hash-chained record of every seal, token issue, open and refused attempt. It holds ids and counts, never row values.

`shift_report.json` | With `--charter`: the exploration set against the deployment sample named by `reference`. Status is `pass` (no shift detected), `fail` or `unverifiable`; without a deployment sample it is `unverifiable`, never `pass`. Holds the classifier and kernel two-sample tests (permutation p-values), per-feature KS or chi-square under Benjamini-Hochberg, subgroup coverage for `sensitive_columns`, and the forward check, which a run reports as skipped because the final-test set is opened only by the final evaluation. Per-period drift is not implemented.

`evaluation.json` (decision keys) | With `--charter` whose charter has a decision block and a binary task: `decision` holds `objective` `chartered_cost`, the cut on the raw probability, the cost model hash and `f11` (calibration check, the path that ran: `bayes`, `recalibrated` or `grid`, rule hash, tier, expected cost with a bootstrap interval, the span of cost ratios on which the rule beats treat all and treat none on development data). `net_benefit` holds the simultaneous band on the locked test set, computed once, with the claim `useful` or `not_useful_in_range`. Costs are inputs: the tier is `attested` only if every cost came from a person.

`framing_link.json` | With `--charter`: whether the charter's target, prediction moment and unit name real columns (`resolved`) or not (`unresolved`). Names are matched to column names only; free text that matches nothing is reported, never rejected, and nothing is gated on it. Reads column names, never values.

`identification_plan.json`, `identification_report.json`, `falsification_report.json`, `sensitivity_report.json`, `causal_claims.json` | With `--charter` whose estimand carries a causal block (charter format 4): the strategy chosen from the charter alone (eligible and ineligible strategies with the missing assumptions or design fields), the design diagnostics computed on `X`, and the claim file with its tier, the five conditions for `confirmed`, the attestors and the hashes of the other four files. A charter no strategy identifies is `not_identified`: no estimate, `action` `refuse_claim`. The estimate, the falsification battery, replication, sensitivity and the tier are computed on the frame the confirmation releases, in the same opening as the bivariate family, and the five files are hashed into the ledger's confirmation row (`scmle claims verify` checks them). When no strategy identifies the charter, or no confirmation set exists, `estimate` is null and the claim is `unverified` or `not_identified`. With declared `attestors` and an `attestations` file (charter format 9), `causal_claims.json` has an `attestations` key (the accepted signed records, the reason each other assumption has none, and the run date they were checked on); the claim rises above `unverified` only if every assumption it needs has an accepted record, and `scmle claims verify` re-checks the signatures (given the key), scopes, dates and the charter's attestor list. With declared `subgroups` (charter format 9), `identification_report.json` has a `subgroups` key (one hypothesis per declared level with estimate, interval, p-value, Holm-adjusted p-value and decision; unestimable levels stay in the family at p = 1) and `causal_claims.json` a short summary; they never change the tier. The key also carries `gate`: `gating` when the Holm family has a current passing certificate in `scmle/certificates/subgroup_certificates.json` (a hypothesis then also has `certified_size`, true from the certified number of rows) and `descriptive` otherwise, with `statement_gate` saying which. With a declared `dag`, `identification_report.json` has a `dag` key (hash, falsification on `X`, refused adjustment members) and `admissibility_table.json` holds the graph rules. A gate counts toward `confirmed` only with a current passing certificate in `scmle/certificates/f10_certificates.json`.

A charter run with a `reconcile` block writes `extract_reconciliation.json`: the totals the charter declared and, under `source_checks`, the same quantities queried from the source database, each compared with the extract.
`charter.json` | The draft charter, unsigned, readable by `scmle charter check` and signable by `scmle charter sign`. Absent when the draft is refused.

`feature_manifest.json`, `ingest_field_provenance.json` | With `--charter` having an `ingest` block and `--ingest-plan`: one record per proposed feature (expression, tables read, cutoff rule, as-of evidence, tier, and why it was dropped, if it was), the declared family size, and the provenance of the kept features that the admissibility stage reads. `ingest_catalog.json`, `grain_report.json`, `join_graph.json` and `ingest_budget.json` are written beside them.

`decision_report.json`, `policy_value.json` | With `--charter` whose decision block is set, on a binary task: the cost-model hash, threshold and net benefit, the fairness satisfaction result per declared constraint (`satisfied`, `not_satisfied` or `not_assessable`), and the off-policy value of the frozen rule from a randomized log (`--logged-action-column`, `--propensity-column`; otherwise `not_assessable`). Computed once on the locked rows. Costs, margins and propensities are inputs.

`decision_threshold.json`, `net_benefit.json` | With a decision block on a binary task: the frozen threshold rule and the net benefit of the rule on the locked rows, each its own file. With `policy_value.json` and `rollout_design.json` their hashes are registered in the custody log (`decision_files` event) and `scmle claims verify` checks them.

`coverage_claim.json`, `coverage_report.json` | With intervals or sets on a regression or classification task: the claim (levels, methods, tolerance, rule) fixed and hashed before the final test rows are released, and the coverage measured on those rows once, with the claim's hash. In a charter run the hash is in the custody log and `scmle claims verify` checks it. A charter whose `uncertainty` block sets `coverage_on_confirmation` (format 11) also writes `coverage_confirmation.json`: the same claim for one served interval or set (`residual` for regression, pooled sets for classification, level 0.9, tolerance 0.02) tested once on the confirmation rows `C` after the model and its calibration are frozen. It holds the covered count, the exact one-sided binomial p-value, and a status `confirmed` (p at most 0.05) or `unverified`; the other methods and levels are described on the same rows without a status. Each declared slice in `coverage_report.json` carries `flag` (below nominal by more than 0.05, Holm over the slices), `flag_certified` and a `flag_gate` that is `gating` only while the stored G5b certificate is current and passing.

`rollout_design.json`, `rollout_decisions.jsonl` | With a rollout plan in the decision block: the plan, its hash, the fixed-horizon sample size and the simulated expected sample number, and a hash-chained log holding the registration of the plan. No experiment ran, so there are no assignments or decisions in it.
`framing_refusal.json` | When refused: the reason (a named column the source lacks, a blocking data check, an unfillable critical slot, or LLM ambiguity above `tau`).
Every LLM-filled field is `unverified` until a person signs the charter, and there is no calibrated `tau` or gold corpus yet, so a replayed LLM draft without `tau` is always refused.

`deployment_ledger.jsonl` | The hash-chained record of the deployment: the charter hash, the policy and its hash, the fingerprints of keys the system holds, then `observe_summary`, `alarm`, `retrain`, `challenger_result`, `promotion_proposal`, `rollback_proposal`, `escalation`, `attestation`, `halt` and `incident` rows (a halt opens one). A challenger is registered before it is scored and its e-LOND decision is replayed on load. An attestation row is bound to one escalation and the hash of its question, carries an expiry, and is refused if it was signed with a key the system holds. The chain shows edits, deletions in the middle and reordering; it cannot show that the newest rows were never removed (compare `scmle loop verify` output with a head kept elsewhere).

`model/` is the checksummed bundle (signed when a signing key is configured; an unsigned bundle is refused unless trusted, and a signed one with no key to verify it is refused even when trusted): `pipeline.joblib` (fitted preprocessing and estimator), `schema.json`, `reference.json` (monitoring reference profile), `conformal.json` (pooled and per-class calibration scores), `novelty.joblib` and `model_manifest.json` (checksums and signature).
`release_evaluation.json` | Whether declared success criteria were met. With none declared it reports `policy_not_declared` and blocks; thresholds are never invented from observed metrics.

`Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `build.sh` | Base image pinned by a digest placeholder that the build refuses until `build.sh` resolves it; non-root user; locked install; credential files excluded; the script that scans the context, resolves the base, builds, scans and attests.

`vuln-policy.json` | The gate policy: block at HIGH and above, with no vulnerability exceptions. One dated waiver lets the `scmle` package itself go unscanned (no index a scanner can query holds it; its dependencies are scanned), and it blocks again once it expires.
The controller never moves the champion alias, and neither does an envelope.
Bad input | An unreadable or malformed file is `rejected` once, escalated, and never retried. The rest of the inbox is still applied.

* **The other ten never-list actions**: reopening a sealed set, changing the charter, editing the ledger or registering late, relaxing a threshold, acting on an unverified stream, answering a flagged high-impact case, suppressing its own alert, changing the labelling policy, deleting or sending externally, and creating or signing an attestation.
They cannot be put in an envelope.
* **A halt by the controller, a rejected file, silence, or a failed training.
An envelope is authority a person signs in advance for an action that is not on the never list.
A use is chained in the ledger **before** the action runs, and the ledger itself refuses a use that is unknown, revoked, out of scope, not covered or over its limit.

Loading a malicious bundle | Loading is **refused unless authentic**: the manifest HMAC-SHA256 signature must verify (`$SCMLE_SIGNING_KEY` or `signing_key=`), or, for an unsigned bundle only, the caller vouches with `trusted=True`; a signed bundle with no key set to verify it is refused even with `trusted=True` | `tests/unit/test_bundle.py`
